summary.headline: Dalmia Q2 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR 746/ton ex-Central (INR 698 reported) as East weakness, fixed-cost under-absorption and fuel costs hit margins.
summary.overview: Volumes rose 3% YoY to 7.1 million tons (4% ex-Central) while East and Northeast demand was weak on floods and rain. Realisation fell about INR 49/ton QoQ, and total costs rose about INR 259/ton ex-Central, mainly fuel (about INR 100/ton), raw materials and under-absorption of fixed costs. Management guided to a higher EBITDA dilution from the Central (Rewa/Jaypee) assets in Q3 but expects core margins to recover on prices, which it says rose about INR 15/bag in Sep-Oct. Exceptional items were INR 339 crore, and leverage has crossed 2x after the JP acquisition.

financial_highlights.change: Central plants diluted by about INR 50/ton
Variable about INR 200/ton; fixed about INR 168/ton
Includes Konark phase-out, captive power impairment (about 97 MW thermal) and INR 57 crore separation scheme

financial_highlights.value: INR 909 crore in Q2; INR 1,420 crore in H1

financial_highlights.change: Down about INR 198 crore after MMDR amendment; about 5% of net worth
RE capacity about 450 MW (from 63 MW five years ago)

segments.name: Core (ex-Central) operations
segments.commentary: Volumes up 4% YoY with South and West growing near double digits; East and Northeast subdued by floods. Realisation down about 1% QoQ in East, with South and West prices steady in Q2.

segments.name: Central India (Rewa / Jaypee assets)
segments.commentary: Rewa mining restarted and clinker line and cement mill in trial runs; target 35-40% utilisation by end FY27. EBITDA dilution about INR 50/ton in Q2, guided to INR 100-125/ton in Q3, with breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27 and Dalmia-standard EBITDA by FY28.

guidance_outlook: Q3 cost headwind of about INR 75-80/ton from fuel at petcoke above USD 180/ton; Q4 not estimated. Fuel cost per million kcal INR 1.66, expected to rise about INR 0.20 in Q3.

Q3 Central EBITDA dilution guided at INR 100-125/ton; management expects fixed-cost under-absorption (about INR 120-140/ton) and the regional mix hit (INR 50-60/ton) to reverse in Q3, with a possible INR 1,000+/ton EBITDA if price gains hold.
Core volume growth for H2 to track industry growth, which management takes as 7-8%.
Clinker capacity of 67 MTPA with Belgaum, Pune and Kadapa; the 75 MTPA target by FY28 is no longer being chased, with JP/BJCL taking capacity to about 70 MTPA.
Leverage to stay below 2x on a sustainable basis; net debt/EBITDA is at a peak after the acquisition and is expected to stay around the 2x line.
Commercial production at Belgaum ahead of peak demand season in Q4 FY27; Pune and Kadapa expected in FY28 (Pune said to come online in Q2 FY28).
capex_capacity: Belgaum clinker line trial runs started ahead of schedule; 3 MTPA cement mill expected to start trial runs in the next couple of weeks; commercial production targeted ahead of Q4 peak season.
Pune and Kadapa progressing as planned; expected in FY28, taking total capacity to about 67 MTPA.
Rewa: mining restarted; clinker line and cement mill ramping under trial runs; Rewa to start commercial production in Q3.
FY27 organic capex guidance unchanged at INR 3,200-3,400 crore; H1 spend INR 1,420 crore. About 20 MTPA of capacity under way at roughly INR 10,000 crore capex.
demand_pricing: Cement demand grew high single digits YoY in the quarter, supported by government capex (central government spent about 42% of budgeted capex in the first 5 months).
South and West growing near double digits; East and Northeast weak on floods and heavy rain, with demand now picking up.
Prices steady in South and West in Q2; East under pressure. Sep and Oct saw price increases of about INR 15/bag above the Q2 average in South and East, and company-wide on average.
Premium offering Weather365 seeing strong response; Konark brand being phased out.
Management did not share regional utilisation or state-level growth, declining to explain share loss questions.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Dalmia's performance weaker than peers ex-Central on volume, price and EBITDA/ton, and will H2 improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about INR 100-120/ton of the hit to fixed-cost under-absorption from weak East/Northeast volumes, and expects this to reverse as demand recovers.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q3 fuel impact of INR 75-80/ton be the peak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot predict peaks; Q3 impact is based on current bookings, and it will not guess Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Could the Central assets reach breakeven and what is the ramp-up strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is breakeven by Q4 FY27 and Dalmia-standard EBITDA by FY28; no utilisation breakeven point was disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q3 INR 100-125/ton dilution an EBITDA or NSR impact, and why is it higher than Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an EBITDA dilution, not NSR; Q2 costs were partly capitalised during trial runs, while Q3 carries full commercial-production costs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the H2 volume growth be above industry growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said core H2 volume growth should track industry (7-8%); internal targets are more aggressive. Central volume ramp-up targets are 35-40% utilisation by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the CFO taking over sales and marketing?
qa_highlights.answer: CMO Navin Tewari moves to an adviser role from 1 January 2027; CFO Yatin Malhotra takes on sales and marketing temporarily. The company intends to appoint a separate CFO later.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt/EBITDA outlook after the JP acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Leverage is at a peak after the acquisition and weak quarterly EBITDA; management is committed to staying around the 2x line and below 2.5x.

qa_highlights.question: What is the intangible asset increase (about INR 150 crore to INR 600 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Interim figure from the JP acquisition in May; mostly mining rights. PPA is under way with a one-year window.

qa_highlights.question: Can Q3 profitability improve QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects INR 150-200/ton from cost and mix recovery, plus about INR 220-230/ton from the INR 15/bag price gain, offset by headwinds; it is hopeful of EBITDA above INR 1,000/ton in Q3.

risks_watch: Petcoke above USD 180/ton and crude above USD 100/bbl: fuel costs of about INR 220/ton war impact in H1 and packing bag costs of about INR 100/ton.
Central India ramp-up: EBITDA dilution rising to INR 100-125/ton in Q3; breakeven by Q4 FY27 is a stated target, not yet proven.
Tamil Nadu MMDR cess still being paid; discontinuation in Assam and Meghalaya from 22 August has not yet translated into cost savings.
Leverage at or above 2x after the JP acquisition; watch net debt/EBITDA against the 2-2.5x comfort range.
Management transition: CMO exit and CFO taking on sales and marketing from 1 January 2027; the company is also running low volumes in the East and losing ground in some markets.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic: management acknowledged weak East volumes, under-absorption and higher costs, while stressing the issues as temporary and expecting a stronger H2 on price increases and mix normalisation. It was evasive on fuel Q4 outlook, state-level market share, regional utilisation and specific one-off quantification.

So I think we get continuity of an internal person to further build on what Navin has created while continuing to get Navin's guidance as we go forward.
we are committed to maintaining leverage below 2x on a sustainable basis

growth.why: H2 FY27 core volume growth guided in line with industry at ~7-8%, backed by Belgaum and Rewa capacity starting in Q3-Q4 and a Sep-Oct price rise of ~INR 15/bag, though East demand weakness, fuel cost headwinds and Central EBITDA dilution of INR 100-125/t in Q3 temper near-term profit growth.
